title: Cut, arrange and retime what is on the timeline
goal: Building a video is mostly cutting: split a take where the fumble is, throw the bad part away, slide what is left, hold on a frame, and speed a boring stretch up. Make all of that direct, reversible and quick, on the timeline, without anything being destroyed.
notes:
Build on docs/design/mocks/pages/video-cut-wt.html, video-freeze-wt.html and video-speed.html. The cut page states the rule this task must keep: "nothing is ever destroyed: a split makes two layers that read the same source". The freeze page says a freeze is not a special object but a clip whose in and out are the same frame, which is a good test of whether the time model from the foundation task is right - if a freeze needs a special case, the model is wrong.

Ripple is the decision most likely to be got wrong by leaving it implicit. Every editor has an answer and they differ; pick one, write it in the design doc, and make delete, trim and move all obey it.

---
SHARED CONTEXT for the video set (the user made video the priority on 2026-09-18).

Their words: "I am shifting priority to video. I want to make sure you are looking at our video usage clickthroughs. These are NOT specs, they are ideas on which we are building on. We are building something better than any other video editor out there. We need a robust set of ways to build video, separate audio, introduce audio, auto caption, slice things, transition and control the effects, interweave components and animate them using animation patterns, etc."

THE CLICKTHROUGHS ARE IDEAS, NOT SPECS. Read them, build ON them, and say in the audit where you went further or differently and why. Fifteen pages exist under docs/design/mocks/pages: video, video-entry-wt, video-cut-wt, video-move-wt, video-zoom-wt, video-freeze-wt, video-title-wt, video-transition-wt, video-transitions, video-captions, video-audio, video-compositing, video-motion, video-speed, and comp-video. Do not start a page from scratch that already exists there.

THE THESIS THEY ALL SHARE, and it should govern every task in this set. Every page says the same thing in its own words:
- "A recording opens the same document with a time dimension, so the transport bar and the timeline dock appear." (video)
- "Audio rides the same time axis as the picture, so a mixer is not a separate app." (video-audio)
- "Captions are not a mode that replaces the app. They are what the Title / Text tool does when the document has time." (video-captions)
- "Compositing is just layers with a rule for how they combine. The stack is the timeline." (video-compositing)
- "Motion is not a separate mode... the same window, on a document that has time... each animated layer gets a lane." (video-motion)
- "A title is a text layer that happens to live in a document with time, so it gets an in and an out." (video-title-wt)
- "A transition is not a filter on a clip. It is a relationship between two clips at a cut." (video-transitions)
- "Retiming is a property of the selected clip, so nothing new appears in the chrome." (video-speed)
- "A freeze is not a special object: it is a clip whose in and out are the same frame." (video-freeze-wt)
- "a key is a value recorded at a moment. There is no keyframe window and no animate mode." (video-move-wt)
So: VIDEO IS NOT A MODE. It is the layer document with time. Anything built as a separate editor, a separate window or a separate model contradicts every page and should not be built that way.

WHAT EXISTS TODAY, and it is the opposite of the thesis, which is why the foundation task comes first. Video is a SEPARATE editor: Sources/Photonz/VideoEditorState.swift and VideoEditorView.swift, one clip at a time, trim and crop and export. TrimTimeline and PlaybackScrubber are SwiftUI views bound to VideoEditorState rather than a reusable model. PhotonzMedia carries VideoExporter and VideoAssetCommit. PhotonzCore has NO notion of time, duration, tracks or keyframes at all. So none of this is "extend the video editor"; it is "give the document time and let the video editor retire into it".

This also settles a question already raised elsewhere: the modes work (work-out-whether-the-app-needs-project-types-at) has as its acid test a component drawn in one mode and placed on a video timeline, and the user said "You can create a component, and then show that on a video timeline" and "you can make an icon and use it in your component". That is only possible if video lives in the layer document. The mocks and the modes direction agree; today's code does not.

And the animation model is already settled by the user, on 2026-09-15: motion is a property of a layer, opening into a timing surface with a lane per moving part. There is NO canned list of named motions. Easing is real curves including a custom one. Two parts of one thing must be able to move out of phase. Whatever time model this set builds must serve that, because an icon animating and a clip moving are the same machinery.

Queue-driven app work targets the next release, and per CLAUDE.md a Current change is not finished until Next has it. Design doc: docs/design/video.md is the source of truth, written by the foundation task.
acceptance: A clip can be split where the playhead is, and the two halves are two PIECES of the same row rather than two rows, each separately selectable, trimmable and stylable, both still reading the same source (corrected by the video design pass 2026-09-19; UX-PATTERNS D18)
Clips can be trimmed from either end, moved, and snapped to each other, to the playhead and to the ends of the document

A clip can be picked up and dropped into a different place in the order, with the timeline showing where it is going to land while you drag, and what plays, what the playhead reads and what an export writes all agree with the new order straight away
Nothing is destroyed: a trim can be pulled back out to the media that is still there, proved by trimming in and then back out to the original length
A frame can be held: a clip whose in and out are the same frame drops onto the timeline like any other clip
A clip can be sped up or slowed down, and the audit shows what happens to its audio when it is
Ripple behaviour is stated and predictable: say what moves when something is removed or lengthened, and make it the same everywhere
Every one of these is a single undo step and the walks prove it
A recording of a real screen capture is cut into a three shot sequence end to end in the audit, which is the proof it is usable rather than merely present
Audit under queue/audits/ with that sequence, and anything rough filed as a follow-up

log.note: deps set: the document gets time first

Triage 2026-09-19: absorbed put-the-pieces-of-a-recording-in-a-different-ord, which asked for exactly the arranging half of this task and was dropped as a duplicate. What it knew, worth keeping: Sources/PhotonzCore/VideoCuts.swift holds VideoCutList with split(atTimeline:), removePiece(at:) and keep(fromTimeline:) and no way to move a piece; the pieces array is already in play order and timeline time is derived from it, so a move is a reorder of that array and everything downstream reads through it. Sources/Photonz/TrimTimeline.swift draws the blocks today. That is the OLD editor, which a-document-can-have-time retires, so build the reorder on the new timeline rather than on the strip, and check the old trim strip does not survive with a second way to do it. Reordering is now an acceptance item here.

ACCEPTANCE ITEM 1 NEEDS CORRECTING BEFORE THIS IS BUILT, from the video design pass (2026-09-19, docs/design/video-surface.md, UX-PATTERNS D18). It says a split makes 'two ordinary layers'. A timeline row is a layer, so two layers means two rows, which means a row per cut and an unusable timeline after five of them. The settled answer: splitting adds a PIECE to the same row, not a row. Each piece is separately selectable, trimmable, movable and carries its own effects, and the layers list shows the layer once with its piece count. 'Pieces' is the word the shipping trim bar already says on screen ('3 pieces'), so it is not a new one to teach. The seam between two pieces is an edit point (comp-video section 02), which is also what a transition attaches to.

The model this needs landed on 2026-09-20 in time-lives-in-the-document-and-a-layer-can-have: a layer carries LayerTime (in, out, and where in its own source that reads from, PhotonzCore/DocumentTime.swift), the document carries durationMS, and the timing strip already DRAWS a bar for a layer that has an in and an out. What is missing and belongs here is the grip: the bar has no gesture on it, so an in and an out cannot yet be dragged, and the design says they are never typed in the panel. LayerTime.withIn/withOut/moved(toInMS:) are written and tested for exactly that, and MotionStripDrag next door is the shape the gesture should take.

SPLIT by the daily triage pass of 2026-09-20. The rules half came out as a-clip-splits-into-pieces-and-the-pieces-can-be and can be built today: splitting a clip into pieces, re-ordering them, the ripple rule, non-destructive trim, a held frame, speed, all pure and tested, with nothing on screen changing. What stays HERE is everything that needs the pending trim-and-send card answered: the grip on the bar so an in and an out are dragged rather than typed, dropping a piece into a different place with the landing shown while you drag, snapping to neighbours and the playhead, and the end-to-end three-shot audit on a real capture. Reason for the split: at the time of the split every p1 in the queue was blocked or waiting on a dependency and nothing served the focus, while the cutting rules depend on the card not at all.

The cutting RULES are built and proved: Sources/PhotonzCore/ClipPieces.swift (45 tests in Tests/PhotonzCoreTests/ClipPiecesTests.swift), landed 2026-09-20 by a-clip-splits-into-pieces-and-the-pieces-can-be. This task is now the GESTURE only. What is already done for you: ClipPiece (sourceInMS + lengthMS + speedPercent, 0 = a held frame) and ClipPieces (the list, laid end to end, never empty), on Layer as an optional 'cuts' read through layer.clipPieces and written through layer.setClipPieces (which keeps layer.time in step). Six document edits, each one History.perform step: splitClip(id, atMS:) and holdFrame(id, atMS:forMS:) take DOCUMENT milliseconds (the playhead); removeClipPiece / moveClipPiece / trimClipStart / trimClipEnd / setClipSpeed take a piece index. clip.playback is what a player and an exporter read. WHAT IS LEFT: (1) the blade, the drag and the piece selection, including which piece is selected after a cut, which the model does not decide; (2) clamping - the edits REFUSE an out-of-range trim rather than guessing, so the drag clamps first with clip.trimStartRange(ofPiece:) / trimEndRange(ofPiece:), whose 'out' is nil when nothing stops it; (3) drawing a held frame, a retimed piece and spare media on the bar; (4) a speed control, which is the only one of the six with no obvious gesture; (5) snapping, which VideoCutSnapping.swift already does in seconds and will want saying in milliseconds. WHAT THE MODEL DELIBERATELY WILL NOT DO: a hole INSIDE a clip cannot be written down at all - remove closes the join and lengthening pushes the rest along, per D18 and video-cut-wt's own filed complaint - so a 'lift leaving a gap' gesture would need a model change and a card first. Also absent on purpose: reverse speed, pitch correction while retiming, ripple across OTHER layers, and roll trim (moving a join without changing the clip's length).

The two ways to change a clip's length are reconciled in docs/design/video-surface.md §10.4, so this task does not have to pick one. Dragging a clip's end with Select is the quick nudge: it moves the in or the out and that is all you see. The Trim tool is a session: both ends held up, the spare at each end drawn with its duration, the numbers in the capsule, and ⎋ putting the clip back the way it was. Same values, same History step, same numbers on screen. That is the same relation as dragging a layer's corner versus entering Crop, so it is not a duplicate to remove.

The foundation for this landed on 2026-09-20 in a-document-can-have-time: a recording opens as a document, a clip is a layer with MovieRef + LayerTime + ClipPieces behind it, and the timeline draws it as a bar. Dragging the bar's ends is YOURS; the trim TOOL in Crop's slot and the retirement of the old recording window are trim-becomes-a-tool-and-the-recording-window-ret. Do not build a second way to change a clip's length without reading docs/design/video-surface.md 10.4, which reconciles the two.

ADVERSARIAL REVIEW, before building (video-cut-wt.html walked as somebody who has never seen it). (1) The mock's step 7-8 CANNOT BE WRITTEN DOWN in the model that landed: 'the left edge moves right and a gap opens where the fumble was', then 'drag the piece left until it snaps against the first half'. ClipPieces lies end to end with no holes inside a clip (D18), so trimming a piece's start ALREADY closes the join and step 8 has nothing to do. That is better, not a shortfall: one gesture where the mock needs two, and no way to leave a gap you did not mean to leave. The green snap line step 8 draws still earns its place, for a different job - lining a WHOLE clip up against another clip, against the playhead and against the ends of the document. (2) The mock makes the blade a TOOL ('Blade is a tool, not a menu command'). Photonz already ships Split at Playhead on plain B in the Video menu, and the design pass has already spent Crop's slot on Trim. A second video-only tool costs a slot and a mode to get out of, and buys only cutting somewhere the playhead is not - which costs you the aim anyway. Shortest version, same value: the playhead IS the cut line, B cuts there, no tool to pick up or put down. Building the command, not the tool. (3) Decorative and cut: the waveform drawn inside the clip (that is video-audio), and the mock's 'no Layers group because the timeline IS the layer list', which the design pass already corrected in video-surface.md 3. (4) REAL RISK found while measuring: the strip's ruler spans the whole document, so an eight second recording about a thousand points wide gives 125 points a second. A piece trimmed to 200ms is 25 points, and two 9 point grips on it leave 7 points of body - so carrying a short piece would be impossible and grabbing its middle would grab an edge instead. The grips have to give way to the body below a minimum width rather than being a fixed 9.

BUILT 2026-09-20. The timeline's clip bar became the surface you cut on. Model: Sources/PhotonzCore/ClipBarDrag.swift (ClipBarGrab .clipStart / .seam(after:) / .carry(piece:) / .body, ClipBarDrag.landing(byMS:) with clamping and catching, PhotonzDocument.clipBarEdges + moveClip + refreshDuration, ClipBarCopy), 30 tests in Tests/PhotonzCoreTests/ClipBarDragTests.swift. App: Sources/Photonz/EditorState+ClipBar.swift (piece pick, split, ripple delete, hold, speed, the drag session, the Escape watch, the drag preview both the strip and the canvas read) and Sources/Photonz/ClipPiecesBar.swift (the bar drawn as pieces, seams, grips that give way to a short piece, hold and speed badges, the green catch band, the capsule). Video menu: Split at Playhead (B) and Delete This Piece now reach the DOCUMENT when the window has one, plus Hold This Frame and a Speed list. Design: docs/design/video-surface.md section 11 states the ripple rule, the gesture rule, what is in your hand after a cut, and where the mock was wrong. Walks: cut-on-the-timeline-walk (9 real pictures) and a-clip-shows-where-it-will-land-walk (6, two of them mid-drag). Audit: queue/audits/2026-09-20-video-cutting.json. 8584 tests pass; every trim, cut, clip, recording and motion-strip walk that can run on a locked screen passes.

REVIEW OF THE BUILT THING, on the real app, and the three things it changed. (1) THE FIRST DESIGN WAS WRONG AND THE WALK CAUGHT IT. Dragging the bar's left end first moved the CLIP along with the edge, so the edge followed the hand perfectly - and left a hole at the front of the recording, because the clip had walked away from nought. The walk's own numbers said so: the timeline still ran 6000 ms after a trim that should have shortened it. Rebuilt the other way: the clip stays where it was put and the bar closes up from its far end, which is the value docs/design/video-surface.md 10.4 says the Trim TOOL writes, and the only one that answers the real job of dragging the dead air off the front of a recording. The edge still follows the hand DURING the drag, because the bar is drawn where the hand has it with the frames being dropped faint in the room that leaves, and it shuts when you let go. (2) THE RULER RESCALED UNDER THE HAND. Sliding a clip two seconds later grew the document from eight seconds to ten WHILE the hand was still down, so the ruler stretched under the bar being dragged - exactly the bug motionStripCycleMS already guards against for a motion bar. Fixed the same way: the document's length is HELD for the life of the drag and only says the new number on release. (3) Mid-carry the highlight stayed on the piece INDEX rather than on the piece, so the bar was drawn in the order it would land in with the wrong piece lit up. Fixed to follow the drop index. Also: B, Delete, Hold and Speed now put the Trim tool down first (committing a session whose handles were moved, dropping an untouched one), because a recording opens with Trim in hand and cutting a bar being shown at its full length would put the cut in the wrong place.

LEFT ROUGH, all of it also in the audit's rough list. Filed as ONE follow-up (a-cut-clip-says-how-many-pieces-it-is-in-and-a-p, p2): the layers list still shows a cut clip as a plain row with no piece count (D18 says it should), and speed has no Properties row (video-speed says retiming is a property of the selected clip). Not filed, recorded here instead: letting go of a trim that shortened a piece reflows the pieces after it, so the bar shifts by the amount you trimmed at the moment you release - every editor does this and the ripple rule requires it, but it is a visible jump and the user may disagree; Hold This Frame has no keyboard shortcut because shift-F walks the Frame slot and option-F fills the flow and nothing free reads as freeze; the joins between pieces are a hairline when the clip is NOT picked, since the grips only come up on the picked clip; snapping has almost nothing to catch on in a one clip recording and will only earn its keep once titles and a second clip are on the timeline. ALSO WORTH KNOWING FOR THE NEXT RUNNER, and it is not an app bug: four walks reported CRASHED with no crash report during this task, including ones that had passed minutes earlier. The cause was two playtest runs overlapping - one run's probe quit kills the other's app, because there is one Photonz Probe bundle and both drive it. Run playtests one at a time; every one of those walks passed when re-run alone.

The timeline's clip bar is now the surface you cut on: split at the playhead (B), ripple delete a picked piece, carry a piece into a different place in the order with the landing drawn while you hold it, drag any edge of the bar, slide a whole clip and catch it on the playhead or another clip, hold a frame, and retime a piece with its sound. Nothing is destroyed. Model in PhotonzCore/ClipBarDrag.swift with 30 tests; surface in EditorState+ClipBar.swift and ClipPiecesBar.swift; ripple rule written into docs/design/video-surface.md 11. Verified: 8584 tests pass, two new walks (cut-on-the-timeline-walk, a-clip-shows-where-it-will-land-walk) pass with 15 real pictures of the window between them, and every trim, cut, clip, recording and motion-strip walk that can run on a locked screen still passes. Audit: queue/audits/2026-09-20-video-cutting.json. Commit a3fe52d7, pushed.
